summary: Semeith Pictures Holdings, LLC (client, Buyer) is buying all outstanding stock of Ashgrove Film Releasing, Inc., an independent film distributor, from Prudond Media Group, Inc. (Seller) for $46,000,000 under a New York-law stock purchase agreement. The SPA has a Closing Date of March 31, 2026. Before Closing, Seller contributes its film library to the Company under a bill of sale. Part of the price goes into escrow. Seller will provide booking, participation accounting and digital delivery services after Closing under a transition services agreement. The Company's President has an existing employment agreement. The SPA's order-of-precedence clause lets each Ancillary Agreement govern its own subject matter. That clause lets flaws in the bill of sale and the escrow agreement control. The folder carries six issues: an uncapped Buyer indemnity for Seller guarantees, a narrowed Film Library definition in the bill of sale, an escrow sole-source clause that caps fraud, fundamental and tax claims, general reps that survive only 120 days, a one-sided TSA assignment clause, and an executive change-of-control consent that the SPA neither discloses nor makes a closing condition.

issues.label: uncapped indemnity
issues.description: Three SPA provisions combine to give Buyer unlimited liability. Article I defines 'Seller Guarantees' as every guarantee, letter of credit or credit support Seller gave for Company obligations, 'whether arising before or after the Closing'. That includes Seller's guarantees of the Company's minimum-guarantee payments to producers. Section 9.3(c) requires Buyer to indemnify Seller for all Losses under the Seller Guarantees. Section 9.5(e) states that the Cap, the Basket and the other limitations in Section 9.5 'shall not apply to claims under Section 9.3(c)'. Read together, these clauses make Buyer the unlimited backstop for guaranty defaults, including obligations the Company incurred before Closing under Seller's ownership. Seller's own indemnity for pre-closing matters is capped.
issues.section: Article I (Seller Guarantees definition), Section 9.3(c) and Section 9.5(e)
detect_terms: whether arising before or after the Closing
shall not apply to claims under Section 9.3(c)
issues.expected_finding: Because the Seller Guarantees definition reaches pre-closing obligations and Section 9.5(e) removes every limitation from the Section 9.3(c) indemnity, Buyer faces unlimited liability for Seller's guarantees, including pre-closing producer minimum-guarantee defaults. The indemnity should be limited to obligations arising after Closing, made subject to a cap, and pre-closing guaranty exposure should be left with Seller.

issues.label: defined term inconsistency
issues.description: SPA Section 1.1 defines 'Film Library' as all released and unreleased titles that Seller or its Affiliates distribute, 'including the 2026 Release Slate'. SPA Section 6.8 requires Seller to contribute the Film Library to the Company before Closing by the Bill of Sale. The Bill of Sale, dated March 30, 2026, redefines 'Film Library' in Section 1 as titles 'theatrically released on or before December 31, 2024'. Only that narrower set is conveyed. SPA Section 11.9 lets each Ancillary Agreement govern its own subject matter, so the Bill of Sale's definition controls what is actually transferred. As a result, the 2025 titles and the 2026 Release Slate stay with Seller even though Buyer pays $46,000,000 for a Company holding the full library.
detect_terms: theatrically released on or before December 31, 2024
issues.expected_finding: The Bill of Sale's narrower Film Library definition governs the conveyance under SPA Section 11.9, so the Company, and therefore Buyer, would not acquire the 2025 titles or the 2026 Release Slate. The Bill of Sale must adopt the SPA definition, or the SPA must make its definition control, before Closing.
issues.section2: Section 1.1 (Film Library definition), Section 6.8 and Section 11.9

issues.label: liability cap carve-out conflict
issues.description: SPA Section 9.5(d) excludes three categories from the 10% Cap: Fraud, breaches of Fundamental Representations, and Taxes. Escrow Agreement Section 7.4 is signed at Closing with Ostrander Trust Company, N.A. It provides that the Escrow Funds are the Buyer Indemnified Parties' 'sole and exclusive source of recovery' for all Losses under Article IX of the Purchase Agreement, 'whether or not subject to the Cap'. SPA Section 11.9 lets the Escrow Agreement govern its own subject matter. Together, these provisions remove the SPA carve-outs. Fraud, Fundamental Representation and Tax claims are confined to the $3,450,000 Escrow Amount, which is below even the $4,600,000 general Cap.
detect_terms: sole and exclusive source of recovery
whether or not subject to the Cap
issues.expected_finding: Read with SPA Section 11.9, Escrow Agreement Section 7.4 limits Buyer's recovery for Fraud, Fundamental Representation and Tax claims to the $3,450,000 escrow, wiping out the Section 9.5(d) carve-outs. Section 7.4 should be revised to preserve direct recovery against Seller for carved-out claims and for amounts above the escrow.
detect_terms2: shall not apply to Losses arising from Fraud

issues.label: indemnity survival gap
issues.description: SPA Section 9.1 provides that the General Representations 'shall survive the Closing until the Initial Release Date' as defined in the Escrow Agreement. Escrow Agreement Section 5.1 sets the Initial Release Date at '120 days following the Closing Date'. With the SPA Closing Date of March 31, 2026, that is July 29, 2026. SPA Section 4.12, the participations and residuals representation, states that producer participation statements are rendered within 90 days after each June 30 and December 31. The first post-closing statement is therefore due September 28, 2026, two months after the general representations expire. Buyer has no practical window to discover inaccuracies in participations, receivables or exhibitor settlements and make a claim.
detect_terms: shall survive the Closing until the Initial Release Date
issues.expected_finding: Computed from the March 31, 2026 Closing Date, the General Representations expire on July 29, 2026. That is before the first participation statement is due on September 28, 2026, so claims are impractical. Survival should run at least 18 months from Closing, independent of the escrow release schedule.

issues.label: unrestricted assignment
issues.description: TSA Section 12.3 bars Buyer, as Recipient, from assigning without Seller's consent. The same section lets Seller, as Provider, assign the TSA or delegate any Service to any Person 'without the consent of Recipient'. That includes a competing distributor. The Services are theatrical booking, participation accounting and digital cinema delivery. They require access to the Company's exhibitor terms, release calendar and participation data. Buyer has no termination right if an assignment occurs.
issues.expected_finding: Seller can freely assign the TSA or delegate Services to a competing distributor, which would gain access to the Company's commercially sensitive booking and release data. Section 12.3 should require Recipient's consent for any assignment or delegation, bar assignment to competitors, and give Recipient a right to terminate.

issues.label: change of control consent
issues.description: SPA Section 4.6 represents that 'No consent, approval or waiver of any Person' is required for the transaction other than Kestrelwave Streaming, Inc.'s consent under its output agreement. SPA Section 7.2(d) conditions Closing only on that one consent. The Company's employment agreement with its President, Marisol Ventrice, says something different in Section 10.2. It provides that the Company shall not undergo a Change of Control, defined to include a sale of more than 50% of its voting stock, 'without the Executive's prior written consent'. If that happens, she may resign for Good Reason within 90 days, receive severance equal to 24 months' base salary, and have rights in the Executive Titles in the library revert to her. The stock sale triggers that clause. The SPA neither discloses the consent nor requires it as a closing condition.
detect_terms: No consent, approval or waiver of any Person
issues.expected_finding: The stock sale is a Change of Control requiring Ms. Ventrice's prior written consent under her employment agreement, which the SPA does not disclose or require. Without that consent, Buyer faces 24 months' severance and reversion of the Executive Titles. Her written consent and waiver should be added to Section 4.6 and made a closing condition under Section 7.2.
detect_terms2: without the Executive's prior written consent
